claims.head: Power against power
claims.call: The Blues’ L1 (Holloway, Thomas and Snuggerud) spends at least 57% of its 5-on-5 time against the Bruins’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Blues keep sending Thomas’s line (Holloway, Thomas and Snuggerud) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jim Montgomery has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Bruins’ first line is Peterka, Zacha and Pastrňák.

claims.gist: At home, Jim Montgomery likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Bruins’ first line.

notes.text: Michael Eyssimont has not played this season. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Connor Clifton has not dressed for the last 5 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Will Borgen has taken his spot beside Nikita Zadorov.
Logan Mailloux is out long term and has not played this season. He is a top-four defenseman. Adam Jiříček has taken his spot beside Philip Broberg.
Dylan Peterson was added to the roster on Oct 11 and has played beside Ross Johnston and Pius Suter.
Aleksanteri Kaskimäki was added to the roster on Oct 18 and has played beside Pius Suter and Otto Stenberg.

STL.head: The matchup suits the Blues
STL.body: St. Louis has been out-chancing opponents lately and has home-ice advantage. The Bruins’ way back in is a penalty kill that holds up.

BOS.head: Not an easy night for the Bruins
BOS.body: St. Louis has been out-chancing opponents lately and has home-ice advantage. The Bruins can pull it off if their penalty kill holds up.

story.head: Strength against strength
paras: The Blues have won two in a row, the last a 6-2 rout of Vegas. The Bruins are 8-2-1.

It’s strength against strength: the Bruins are one of the league’s best for chance quality, but the Blues are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. At home, Jim Montgomery likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Bruins’ first line.
